title: About XUYI | Plastic Drinkware Manufacturer in Taizhou, China | XUYI Bottles
description: XUYI Bottles (台州市旭一家居用品有限公司) is a Taizhou, China supplier of reusable plastic sports bottles, kids bottles, water jugs and shakers for wholesale and OEM/ODM projects.
h1: Plastic Drinkware, Built Around Your Project
lead: XUYI Bottles is the trading name of 台州市旭一家居用品有限公司 (Taizhou Xuyi Household Goods Co., Ltd.), a Taizhou, Zhejiang–based supplier dedicated exclusively to reusable plastic drinkware — sports bottles, kids' bottles, large-capacity jugs, and shaker bottles for wholesale, OEM, and ODM projects.

We operate our own production facility and work with a vetted network of partner manufacturers for specialized processes. Every engagement follows the same discipline: the right model, verified against your specification, before anything goes into production.

taizhou: Taizhou — Huangyan district in particular — is widely recognized for mold-making and plastics manufacturing. For a bottle buyer, that geography is practical, not decorative: tooling expertise, component suppliers, and process know-how are concentrated in the region. XUYI operates inside that ecosystem, so a lid redesign, a new closure mechanism, or a packaging revision can be prototyped, tested, and revised through a coordinated supply chain.
workflowTitle: How We Work — A Five-Gate Workflow
workflowIntro: Sourcing problems often begin before production: a wrong model, a material assumption, or artwork approved against a rendering rather than a physical bottle. Our workflow addresses those risks in order.
workflow: Intended users, destination market, order volume, and timeline. A retailer needing shelf-ready packaging and a distributor planning a long-term model run get different questions and different answers.
Capacity, lid mechanism, component materials, and dimensions are checked against the actual catalog model and its photographs, never against a rendering.
Colors, artwork, decoration method, and packaging are confirmed for the selected model. Structural changes go through feasibility review before any tooling discussion.
Samples, an agreed quality scope, and order records are signed off. What gets tested, how it gets tested, and what evidence the buyer receives are decided before production.
Carton measurements, packing lists, markings, documents, and transport terms are reconciled against the approved order before goods move.
manufacturing: A plastic bottle is not one process — it is several, and each one answers to the design. Bottle bodies are formed through the molding process appropriate to the polymer and geometry, including blow-molding where specified. Caps, handles, and other parts may be injection-molded. Decoration, assembly, and packing follow as separate, checkable stages.

We describe the production route the chosen bottle will actually follow, model by model. When a specialized process takes place at a vetted partner facility, the route, responsibility, and approval checkpoints are identified before production.
qualityLead: Quality is organized around an agreed buyer specification sheet. Product and shipment checks are chosen for the model and purchase order.
quality: Actual volume, dimensions, finish, and visible defects
Fit, open/close operation, and defined leak checks
Placement, color accuracy against reference samples, and wear resistance
Count, labeling, cushioning, and transit protection
Destination-market requirements for the exact part and use, supported by matching declarations or scoped laboratory reports
qualityAfter: Where relevant to the product and order, inspection work includes color assessment, print-wear evaluation, temperature and humidity exposure, transport vibration, carton edge-crush, and packaging burst-strength checks. Methods, sample scope, and reporting are agreed before testing. We share the actual results rather than claiming every product carries the same certificate.
noClaims: Plastic drinkware is all we do — focus is a feature.
Our catalog images are photographs of our catalog. What you see is the model we discuss.
Where a figure isn't yet verified — a rate, a capacity, a timeline — we mark it "to be confirmed," and then we confirm it. We'd rather answer precisely late than impressively wrong.
